national-museum-country-life: The national museum of Irish rural life, in grounds with gardens and a mill — free entry.
westport-house: A Georgian mansion of the Browne family with an adventure park, a small zoo and historic grounds.
keem-bay: A horseshoe-shaped bay of white sand, repeatedly voted among Ireland's most beautiful beaches.
achill-island: Ireland's largest island, linked by a bridge, with the Croaghaun cliffs, wild beaches and the village of Keel.
croagh-patrick: St Patrick's holy mountain (764 m), with an annual pilgrimage and views over Clew Bay and its 365 islands.
eagles-flying: Ireland's birds-of-prey centre with flying displays of eagles, falcons and owls.
drumcliffe: A 6th-century monastic site with a high cross and round tower, where W.B. Yeats is buried.
lissadell-house: The Gore-Booth family mansion, linked to Constance Markievicz and Yeats, with gardens and an exhibition gallery.
sligo-abbey: A 13th-century Dominican abbey, the only one in Ireland with its original medieval high altar preserved.
queen-maeves-trail-knocknarea: A trail up to Queen Medb's cairn of stones on the summit of Knocknarea, with views of Sligo and the Atlantic.
carrowmore-megalithic-cemetery: Ireland's largest concentration of megalithic tombs, over 5,500 years old, beneath the gaze of Knocknarea.
strandhill-beach: A surfing beach at the foot of Knocknarea, with surf schools, seaweed baths and a famous sunset.
benbulben: A limestone table mountain and symbol of Sligo, immortalised by Yeats, with a ridge trail and an easy walk at its base.
ards-forest-park: A forested peninsula with beaches, Franciscan ruins and coastal trails facing Sheephaven Bay.
errigal: Donegal's highest mountain (751 m), with a steep climb and a panorama over the Poisoned Glen.
grianan-of-aileach: A 6th/7th-century stone fort on top of Greenan Mountain, former seat of the kings of Tyrconnell.
fanad-head-lighthouse: An iconic 1817 lighthouse among the Fanad beaches, with interior tours and lighthouse accommodation.
malin-head: Ireland's northernmost point, with a Napoleonic signal tower, Star Wars filming locations and Atlantic views.
donegal-castle: A restored O'Donnell fortress with an adjoining Jacobean mansion, in the centre of Donegal Town.
sliabh-liag: Sea cliffs of almost 600 metres — among the highest in Europe — with the One Man's Pass trail.
glenveagh-national-park: Ireland's second-largest national park, with a castle, gardens, glacial valleys and reintroduced golden eagles.
sliabh-beagh: A bogland plateau on the border with Northern Ireland, with trails, a viewpoint and a visitor centre.
patrick-kavanagh-centre: A centre dedicated to the poet Patrick Kavanagh in the old church of Inniskeen, his birthplace.
carrickmacross-lace-gallery: A studio and gallery of the famous Carrickmacross lace, the technique used in the wedding dress of Diana, Princess of Wales.
monaghan-county-museum: Ireland's first county museum, award-winning, with collections on crafts, conflict and rural life.
